Joint Wald tests for model terms and coefficient contrasts

Source: R/wald-test.R
fastglm_wald_test.Rd

Tests specified linear combinations of regression coefficients in a fitted model. A factor or interaction can be tested as a complete formula term, and a named contrast can compare coefficients without refitting.

fastglm_wald_test(
  object,
  terms = NULL,
  contrast = NULL,
  null = 0,
  vcov. = NULL,
  component = "all"
)

Arguments

object

a fastglm GLM (including negative-binomial and streaming GLMs), ordinal, truncated-count, hurdle, zero-inflated, or two-part fit.

terms

formula terms, or coefficient names for a matrix fit, to test jointly. The default selects all formula terms or all matrix coefficients except a coefficient named (Intercept). For ordinal models it selects location slopes. A nonparallel ordinal term includes its slopes at all thresholds. Formula terms refer to their fitted design columns; a main-effect test with interactions depends on their coding and reference values and is not a test of every effect involving that variable. For two-component models, names select complete terms in the selected component(s), or unprefixed coefficient names for matrix fits. With component="all", each term is tested wherever it occurs. A term must occur in at least one selected component.

contrast

numeric vector or matrix specifying linear combinations. Named columns may select a subset of coefficients in any order; omitted columns have weight zero. Unnamed contrasts must follow coef(object). Each matrix row specifies one hypothesis. Use either terms or contrast. For two-component models, named contrasts use the count_ and zero_ prefixes returned by coef(object). A contrast spanning components requires component="all"; its interpretation depends on their coefficient scales.

null

hypothesized value for each selected coefficient or contrast; a scalar is repeated across hypotheses. The default is zero.

vcov.

optional coefficient covariance matrix, or a function of object returning one. The default uses vcov(object). A named matrix must contain all coefficient names; its order may differ. Robust or cluster covariance can be supplied from fastglm_vcov().

component

"all" (default), "count", or "zero" for two-component models. Two-part fits also accept "positive" for the positive-amount component and "binary" for the positive-outcome probability. The zero component describes the probability of a positive outcome for hurdle and two-part fits, and structural-zero probability for zero-inflated fits. Single-component and ordinal fits use "all".

Value

A fastglm_wald_test inheriting from fastglm_test and htest, with statistic, degrees of freedom, p-value, availability, contrast estimates, standard errors, null values, and the contrast matrix and its covariance. Print the object directly or use as.data.frame() for numeric extraction.

Details

For contrast matrix L, coefficient estimate b, and covariance V, the statistic is (L b - null)' solve(L V L', L b - null). Its reference is chi-square with one degree of freedom per independent contrast. This is a first-order approximation requiring asymptotically normal, estimable coefficients and a consistent covariance for the sampling design. It is not a finite-sample F test or a likelihood-ratio test.

Mean-bias-reduced estimates use the same first-order convention. Sparse outcomes, extreme effects, and few independent clusters can make the approximation inaccurate. Tests of regression coefficients do not assess the common-slope restriction; use fastglm_po_test() for that hypothesis.

Nonconvergence, collapsed ordinal categories, nonestimable contrasts, and missing or numerically singular contrast covariance return an unavailable result with an explanation. Degrees of freedom are not reduced silently. For aliased GLM coefficients, estimability is checked against the retained dependence between design columns. No generalized inverse is used. Tests concern regression coefficients, excluding dispersion or size parameters. An estimated negative-binomial size at its numerical boundary returns an unavailable result. Truncated, hurdle, and zero-inflated fits use regression covariance accounting for estimated size in regular fits. For fastglm_nb(), the default retains its conventional fixed-size GLM covariance; to use joint observed information, supply the regression block of vcov(object, full=TRUE). Supplied covariance must contain all regression coefficients, including both components when applicable, even for a selected-component test. Cross-component covariance is retained; it is not replaced with independent component calculations. The covariance restrictions of fastglm_vcov() continue to apply, including its restriction on adjusted two-part fits.

Examples

fit <- fastglm_ordinal(Sat ~ Infl + Type + Cont, MASS::housing,
                      weights=Freq, firth=TRUE)
fastglm_wald_test(fit, terms="Type")
#> Joint Wald test
#> Terms: Type
#> Estimation: mean bias reduction
#> Covariance: model-based
#> 
#>  Statistic df p-value
#>       54.2  3 < 1e-04
#> 
#> Tested contrasts:
#>               Estimate Std. Error    Null
#> TypeApartment  -0.5701     0.1187  0.0000
#> TypeAtrium     -0.3650     0.1568  0.0000
#> TypeTerrace    -1.0867     0.1515  0.0000
#> 
#> Note: First-order chi-square approximation; validity depends on coefficient
#>   estimability and the covariance assumptions.
fastglm_wald_test(fit, contrast=c(InflHigh=1, InflMedium=-1))
#> Joint Wald test
#> Estimation: mean bias reduction
#> Covariance: model-based
#> 
#>  Statistic df p-value
#>      33.82  1 < 1e-04
#> 
#> Tested contrasts:
#>            Estimate Std. Error   Null
#> Contrast 1   0.7194     0.1237 0.0000
#> 
#> Note: First-order chi-square approximation; validity depends on coefficient
#>   estimability and the covariance assumptions.
